Definition: from G473 and the middle voice of G2983; to take hold of in turn, i.e. succor; also to participate:--help, partaker, support.
BiblicalUsage: To take hold of in turn, to succour, to help. Paul tells the strong to support the weak, remembering the Lord's words that it is more blessed to give than to receive, and the Lord takes hold of Israel His servant in remembrance of His mercy. The word is a hand laid on the shoulder of the weak.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for taking hold to help carries no teaching of its own; its beauty is the Lord's, that He took hold of Israel His servant and remembered His mercy.
